summary: Iterates over an entry array and broadcasts each entry's collision event over the network, skipping entries for which FlagBitTest(2) returns non-zero. The iteration count is read from this[3973] (byte offset 0x3E14) and the entry array base is this + 3869 (byte offset 0x3C74). Returns the count value after the loop.

operations.description: Read the entry count from this[3973] (byte offset 0x3E14) into result and initialize the loop index to 0.
Guard on count > 0; when the count is zero the loop body never runs and the function returns immediately.
do-while loop over the count entries, starting at the entry array base this + 3869 (byte offset 0x3C74) and advancing one element per iteration.
Each iteration test a flag bit via FlagBitTest(2); the broadcast is skipped when it returns non-zero.
When the flag bit test returns zero, broadcast the current entry's collision event via CollisionEventNetworkBroadcast(*v4).
Re-read this[3973], increment the loop index, advance the entry pointer v4, and advance the secondary pointer v5 (this + 229, stepped by 35 dwords) until the index reaches the count.
Return the count value stored in result.
Called by NetworkUIUpdate (0x00462848) as part of the network update path.

clean_pseudocode: int result = this[3973];  /* dword index -> byte offset 0x3E14 */
unresolved: Meaning of flag bit 2 tested by FlagBitTest and why a set bit suppresses the broadcast is unknown.
The secondary pointer v5 (this + 229, advanced by 35 dwords) is advanced but its value is unused in the loop body; its purpose is unknown.
Entry element type and the structure of the collision event broadcast are unknown.
